checkpoints.notes: 5 concepts brainstormed and scored, deliberately distinct from Cycle 1's lineup; Echo Maze selected (sonar-reveal stealth-puzzle), Tether Tag as fallback.

Single-file HTML5 canvas architecture: grid maze, fog-of-war reveal via ambient radius + ping pulses, simple guard FSM (patrol/investigate), win/lose on exit/catch. Tunable constants and testing plan defined.

Self-contained playable prototype: deterministic serpentine-maze stealth game, fog-of-war reveal, BFS-based guard patrol/investigate AI (an upgrade over the design doc's ad-hoc steering fallback -- simpler and more robust), win/lose states, restart. No build step, no external assets/deps. Live (non-cached) test-hook getters exposed via window.__echoMaze, applying the cycle-1 lesson about stale snapshot hooks.

Automated Playwright/headless-Chromium end-to-end tests: smoke checks (no console errors, canvas renders, movement/ping affect state) plus two full deterministic playthroughs -- known-solvable path reaches 'won', deliberate detour into the guard room reaches 'lost'. All 6/6 checks PASS. Found and fixed a bug in the test's own movement-settling logic (edge-hugging cell releases blocking the next connector) during development -- game code needed no changes. Investigate-state trigger and manual feel/balance playtesting flagged as follow-ups, not covered by automated tests.
